title: Stabilize routing during rapid capacity churn to avoid incompatible-variant failovers
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Summary: A high-severity capacity event on 2026-02-22 exposed a race between policy evaluation, policy cache TTL refresh, and fallback selection logic. During rapid cross-region capacity churn, the routing control plane routed traffic to an incompatible model variant (quantized-int4 variant missing a serialization shim) as a fallback, causing a subset of requests to fail with deserialization errors and amplified downstream retries that burned capacity. This ticket tracks the follow-up remediation, telemetry improvements, and preventive controls.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-22T03:08:12Z - Canary alerts: latency SLOs degraded in eu-west-1 for model-family 'redwood-medium-v2'.
2026-02-22T03:09:40Z - Router automated fallback kicked in: regional pool depleted, fallback policy initiated cross-region reroute to eu-central-1.
2026-02-22T03:10:05Z - Telemetry shows variant swap to 'redwood-medium-v2-quant-int4' as primary fallback; this variant lacks a recently-introduced compatibility shim for streaming chunks.
2026-02-22T03:10:20Z - 503/decoding errors spike for customer requests routed to fallback variant; client SDKs retry aggressively, increasing request fanout.
2026-02-22T03:11:30Z - On-call routed emergency throttles and pinned affected customer routes to a safe model variant in eu-central-1; error rate begins to decline.
2026-02-22T03:45:00Z - Incident declared Major. Initial mitigation: temporary adjustment of fallback policy priority and emergency rollout of compatibility shim to quant int4 nodes.
2026-02-22T06:30:00Z - Error rates returned to baseline; post-incident data collection begins.
2026-02-23 - Post-incident engineering review and initial hypotheses captured; telemetry gaps identified.
detection_and_mitigation: Detection: Canary SLO alerting combined with customer error-rate dashboards detected the issue within 2 minutes of onset.
Mitigation: Emergency throttle on retries, manual override of routing policy to exclude quantized-int4 variants, and hotfix deployment of the streaming compatibility shim to affected hosts.
Mitigations avoided a wider outage but revealed weaknesses in policy evaluation ordering and cache staleness handling.
root_cause: A policy evaluation race + stale policy cache TTL allowed an older fallback priority list to be used while a canary variant rollout was in progress. The stale fallback prioritized a quantized variant that did not have a deployed streaming compatibility shim. Combined with aggressive client-side retry behavior and automatic re-routing by the control plane, this produced a feedback loop that increased load on fallback pools and triggered further cross-region churn.
action_items: (Aisha) Implement atomic policy versioning in the routing control plane so fallback decisions reference a policy fingerprint rather than per-node cache items. Due: 2026-03-12
(Sofia Alvarez) Add a fast preflight compatibility check before promoting a variant as an allowed fallback (verify runtime features like streaming, tokenization hooks). Due: 2026-03-19

(Marcus Chen) Harden fallback selection to prefer compatibility over lower-cost variants when requests are mid-flight; add a grace window to avoid swapping variants for in-flight sessions. Due: 2026-03-26
(Diego Morales) Rate-limit automated retries at the router ingress when a route sees >5% decoding errors in 60s to prevent amplification. Due: 2026-03-12
(Reliability) Implement a per-variant health signal that includes serialization/streaming self-checks and surface as a gating signal for policy prioritization. Due: 2026-04-02

(Observability) Add structured telemetry: record policy fingerprint, variant fingerprint, and policy-cache TTL at the time of decision for every routed request. Backfill for the last 30 days. Due: 2026-03-18
(SRE) Create runbook for cross-region capacity churn that includes immediate mitigation steps: isolate failing variant, pin route, and toggles for fallback ordering. Due: 2026-03-09
(Product) Re-evaluate default fallback priorities for hosted customers and document compatibility guarantees for quantized variants in the model catalog. Due: 2026-03-30
comments: 2026-03-01 - Marcus Chen: Created ticket after cross-functional review. Prioritized P0 due to high customer impact and capacity burn observed.
2026-03-03 - Aisha Patel: Started spike to enumerate cache invalidation points. Found two code paths that reconcile policy lists independently (control-plane push vs agent pull).
2026-03-05 - Sofia Alvarez: Prototype preflight compatibility probe implemented; needs integration tests for streaming and chunking behaviors.
2026-03-08 - Diego Morales: Deployed preliminary ingress retry limiter to beta region; saw 12% reduction in fallback amplification during synthetic chaos tests.
2026-03-10 - Marcus Chen: Design review with product and SRE scheduled; plan to roll changes in three phased releases to limit blast radius.
status_notes: In Progress: policy versioning spike 60% complete; compatibility preflight tests passing in staging. Next milestone: wire policy fingerprint into telemetry and run chaos injection in eu-west-1 replica.
notes_for_pm: Product should weigh compatibility guarantees vs cost benefits for quantized variants. Recommend adding explicit compatibility labels on model catalog entries so console and API clients can surface warnings.
operational_risks: Short-term: Rolling changes to routing increase complexity; require tight coordination with SRE for canarying.
Long-term: If compatibility gating is too strict, customers may see fewer low-cost variants and higher unit cost.
